title: Code Releases

panels.title: Last Deploy
panels.description: Since the most recent deploy in any environment. Dated from the first agent run under the new code_id, so it lags the real deploy by up to one run interval. Mid-incident this is the tile that answers "was it us".

panels.title: Nodes on Old Code

targets.expr: sum(puppet_code_id_nodes{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"} unless on(alias, environment, code_sha) puppet_code_id{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"}) or (vector(0) and on() (count(puppet_code_id_nodes{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"}) > 0))

panels.description: Nodes still running a code version that is not their environment's current one. Non-zero right after a deploy is normal and drains as nodes run: read it against Last Deploy. Still non-zero after a full run interval means a subset never took the new code.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Nodes whose latest run under the current code failed. This is the tile that says the release broke something.

panels.title: Correcting Drift
panels.description: Nodes applying corrective changes under the current code. A rise after a deploy means the release is fighting drift it introduced. PE only: FOSS reports carry no corrective flag, so a truthful zero.

panels.title: Changed
panels.description: Nodes the current code actually changed, right now. Per-release observed counts, which do not decay as agents re-run, are in the ledger below.

panels.title: Environments With Code
panels.description: Environments with code deployed by Code Manager. Fewer than the Environments board counts, because an environment Code Manager has not deployed to carries no code_id.

panels.title: What Each Release Did

targets.expr: 1000 * ((sum by (deployment) (puppet_deploy_start_epoch)) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"}))

(puppet_deploy_end_epoch - on(deployment) puppet_deploy_start_epoch) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})

value.title: Open this commit in the control repo

panels.description: One row per deployment that started inside the time range, newest first. Predicted is CD4PE impact analysis for that release; observed is what PuppetDB recorded under it. Blank predicted means the pipeline ran no analysis; blank observed means it has not been counted yet, or ran under a deployment policy that cannot be counted exactly. Both pairs are in the same units: resources are distinct resources on both sides, not per-node change events. Each delta is observed minus predicted. **A delta is a prompt to look, not a verdict, because the two sides do not measure the same thing.** Predicted counts what the catalog would change; observed counts what the agents actually applied, and a resource already in the desired state is predicted and never applied. And observed counts everything that changed on those nodes during the deployment, which is not the same as what the release caused: anything else the estate did in that window lands in the count too. **Two specific inflations are known, measured, and deliberately not subtracted here, because this panel reports what PE reports.** Predicted counts collected exported resources as changes: if the exported set moved between the stored catalog and the fresh one, every collected Host, Sshkey, concat fragment or scrape job reads as added. A one-file commit legitimately predicted eleven resources on this estate, ten of them collected exports. pdctng contributes to this itself through pdctng::export_scrape_job. Observed on a production release carries a floor of roughly four resources whenever the node set includes the primary, which it usually does: the primary converges its own pg_hba.conf, pg_ident.conf and infra_inventory.txt inside the deployment window, deterministically and on every rolling deployment. Those are real changes PE really recorded, and they are caused by the deployment without being caused by the commit. Neither is a corrective change, so the corrective/intentional split does not separate them.

panels.title: Predicted Against Observed

targets.expr: (puppet_deploy_observed_nodes - on(deployment) puppet_deploy_predicted_nodes) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})

(puppet_deploy_observed_resources - on(deployment) puppet_deploy_predicted_resource_changes) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})

((sum by (deployment) (puppet_deploy_predicted_nodes) * 0 + 1) or (sum by (deployment) (puppet_deploy_info) * 0)) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})

panels.description: The impact analysis against what PuppetDB recorded, one row per deployment, newest first. Predicted is CD4PE impact analysis for that release; observed is what ran under it. Prediction says whether an impact analysis ran at all: a release deployed straight by Code Manager has no pipeline behind it and never had one, which is why the predicted columns can be empty for a whole window. Blank observed means it has not been counted yet, or ran under a deployment policy that cannot be counted exactly. Both pairs are in the same units: resources are distinct resources on both sides, not per-node change events. Each delta is observed minus predicted. **A delta is a prompt to look, not a verdict, and What Each Release Did above carries the full reasoning for why.** The two sides do not measure the same thing, two specific inflations are known and deliberately not subtracted, and neither is a fault in the release.

panels.title: Nodes Skipped
panels.description: Nodes still reporting under an ephemeral CD4PE environment, which an impact analysis triggered now would drop from its node list without saying so. Normal for up to a run interval after a rolling deployment and drains on its own. While it is non-zero, a prediction under-counts by roughly this many nodes: let it reach zero before reading one, or before triggering a pipeline you mean to measure. The analysis reports SUCCEEDED either way.

panels.title: Which Nodes, and What They Are Still Filed Under
panels.description: One row per node whose latest report is still filed under an ephemeral environment. Target is the environment the deployment was aimed at, and is blank once that deployment has aged out of the event store — the node is still listed, because an analysis will skip it either way. Empty is the healthy steady state.

panels.title: Change Events

targets.expr: sum((puppet_deploy_observed_changes) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})) or (vector(0) and on() (count((puppet_deploy_info) and on(deployment) ((1000 * puppet_deploy_start_epoch) >= ${__from} <= ${__to}) and on(deployment) (puppet_deploy_info{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})) > 0))

panels.description: Resource change events recorded across the deploys in this window, counted per node per resource: the blast radius, and the largest of the three impact numbers by construction. Predicted Against Observed above counts *distinct resources* instead, because that is the only unit an impact analysis can be compared in. Zero means deploys landed and changed nothing; empty means no deploys in the window at all.

panels.title: Compilers Synced

defaults.noValue: No Code Manager token, or not collected

panels.description: Whether Code Manager has pushed the deployed code to every file-sync client. A different question from whether the deploy succeeded, and the one that explains a compiler serving stale catalogues after a good deploy. No means the table beside this names which client is behind.

panels.title: File Sync Clients
panels.description: Every file-sync client and whether it holds the deployed code, with how long since it last checked in. A client that is synced but has not checked in for a long time is the compiler-went-away signal: it is not behind, it is gone, and the tile beside this still reads Yes because nothing is unsynced.

panels.title: Last File Sync

defaults.noValue: No Code Manager token, or not collected

panels.description: When Code Manager last pushed each environment to the file-sync clients, from its own record rather than from the reports. Read against Time Since Deploy below: a recent sync under a stale report date means the code landed and nothing has run since.

panels.title: Rollout Progress

targets.expr: sum by (alias, environment) (puppet_code_id_nodes{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"} and on(alias, environment, code_sha) puppet_code_id{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})

sum by (alias, environment) (puppet_code_id_nodes{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"} unless on(alias, environment, code_sha) puppet_code_id{environment=~"${environment}",alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"})

panels.description: Nodes on their environment's current code against nodes still on an older one, stacked. A deploy shows as the old band draining into the new one. A band that stops draining is the straggler set the headline tile is counting.

panels.title: Current Code
panels.description: What Code Manager says each environment should be running. code_sha comes from File Sync content, not from git. It is not a commit SHA and does not link to one.

panels.title: Nodes by Code Version
panels.description: What is actually running. More than one row for an environment means a rollout in progress, or stalled. code_sha comes from File Sync content, not from git. It is not a commit SHA and does not link to one.

panels.title: Time Since Deploy
panels.description: Per environment. A figure sitting suspiciously close to the exporter start time means the reports aged past PuppetDB report-ttl and there was no history left to date the deploy with. Dated from the reports; **Last File Sync** above dates the same deploys from Code Manager itself, and the two disagreeing is the interesting case.

panels.title: Failed In The Queue Now
panels.description: **Right now, not over the range**, which is the difference between this tile and the Deploy Errors count below it. Code Manager reports the state of its queue at this instant, so a deploy that failed at 2am and was retried successfully at 6am is not here — it is in the log panels. **Zero here beside a non-zero Deploy Errors is the normal healthy reading**: things broke and were fixed. Zero here beside a *rising* Deploy Errors is the one to chase. **Zero is emitted rather than absent**, so this really does mean none rather than "nobody asked"; with no `pdctng::code_manager_token` set the tile says so instead, because the status API refuses the agent certificate.

panels.title: In Flight Now
panels.description: Deploys queued, starting or running at this instant. **A number that does not move across several refreshes is a wedged queue**, which is the failure this whole row exists for: it produces no failed report, no log line and no change anywhere else on this board, so a stuck deploy and a quiet afternoon look identical without it.

panels.title: Environments Failing Now
panels.description: Which environments have a deploy sitting in a failed state **at this instant**. Empty means nothing is stuck, and is the normal reading even on a day when the log panels below show errors — those describe the selected range and this describes now. **The git error is deliberately not here**: it is unbounded text and holding it as a label would mint a series per message, so the count is the metric and the message stays in the console and in the log lines below.

panels.title: Oldest Stuck Failure
panels.description: How long the oldest **currently stuck** failure has been sitting there. Age is what separates a deploy that has just failed and will be retried from one nobody has looked at since Tuesday. Absent when the queue is clear, which is the answer you want and is not the same as no deploy having failed recently — for that, read the Deploy Errors panels below.

panels.title: Deploys per Week: Pipeline vs All Code Changes
panels.description: Pipeline deployments against every code_id an environment has actually run. Where CD4PE deploys everything these agree, so a gap is code arriving by some other route. An estate not using CD4PE has no pipeline line at all, which is honest rather than a fault.

panels.title: Change Failure Rate
panels.description: Finished deployments that did not end in success, over all finished deployments. A deployment still running is not counted. Cancelled is not counted as a failure: stopping a release on purpose is not the release going wrong. Empty means no deployment ledger, which is not the same as zero failures.

panels.title: Fleet Running the Current Code
panels.description: Nodes on the environment's current code_id over the environment's node count. 100% is converged.

panels.title: How Long the Deploy Took
panels.description: The deployment's own duration, per release. Settled: a finished deployment's number never moves again, which is what makes these comparable across releases.

panels.title: Time the Fleet Has Been Catching Up
panels.description: Seconds since the deploy, shown only while nodes are still picking the code up. Empty means every environment is converged, which is the answer you want: this panel is deliberately blank on a healthy estate.

description: What is deployed, whether it has reached everything, and what it did. Requires Code Manager; bare r10k sites will see no data.
